newsitem.title: IRAQ: UNICEF, Iraq launch large vaccination campaign.
newsitem.headline: UNICEF, Iraq launch large vaccination campaign.

text.p: The United Nations children's fund UNICEF, in cooperation with Iraq's Health Ministry, on Tuesday launched a country-wide campaign to immunise more than three million Iraqi children against polio.
"We are very confident that by the year 2000, polio will be eradicated in Iraq," Philippe Heffinck, UNICEF representative in Iraq, told reporters.

The World Health Organisation said last week Iraq's health system was close to collapse and that medicines and other life-saving supplies scheduled for importation under Baghdad's "oil-for-food" deal with the United Nations had not arrived.
"The health situation in Iraq has deteriorated over the last years especially malnutrition, acute respiratory infections and diarrhoeal diseases," Heffinck said.

Crippling United Nations sanctions imposed on Iraq after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait have left many Iraqis desperate for food and medical supplies. Medical imports are exempt from the sanctions but Iraq has little cash to pay for them.
Under the oil agreement put into effect in December, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion of oil over six months and use most of the money to buy food and medicine for its more than 20 million people.

Health Minister Umeed Madhat Mubarak said despite the serious health situation in Iraq, medical supplies under the oil deal were being delayed by the U.S. and British delegations dealing with this at the United Nations.
UNICEF has funded most of the children's health programmes in Iraq since the Gulf War which forced Iraqi troops out of Kuwait in 1991.
